literal.prompt: Какой парк Эквадора охраняет гигантских черепах, морских игуан и вьюрков Дарвина?

literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO Galápagos L46-L47 locates the archipelago off Ecuador and names marine iguanas and giant tortoises; L53/L55 explicitly names Darwin finches; L59 establishes park protection of 97% of land. Komodo L44 is Indonesian and Chitwan L48-L49 Nepali, so those do not match the specified fauna/place. A complete Ranthambore context was not obtained. Independently, islands-013 already tests the Galápagos/Darwin/giant-tortoise recognition; park wording does not cure it.
literalGroups.locator: Galápagos L46-L59; Komodo L44-L47; Chitwan L48-L49; exact current islands-013 MAIN in peer snapshot

literalGroups.literal: Это Галапагосский национальный парк. Изоляция островов способствовала формированию множества уникальных видов.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The explicit park answer is supported by land protection at UNESCO L59. Extreme isolation contributing to unusual fauna is stated at L5/L47; the explanation says contributed, not the sole cause. Two sentences and no unsupported date or mechanism are introduced.

literalGroups.literal: Галапагосский национальный парк охраняет большую часть суши архипелага и его эндемичную фауну.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO L59 puts 97% of emerged surface under National Park status, so most land is accurate. The endemic fauna is documented at L55-L56. Coverage of most land is an additional own-park fact beyond the prompt fauna clues and key label; no percentages or population figures from snippets are needed.

literalGroups.literal: Комодо — индонезийский парк, охраняющий комодского варана, островные ландшафты и окружающие морские экосистемы.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO L44 places Komodo NP in Indonesia, L45-L47 describes terrestrial/marine ecosystems and its dragon, and L57 identifies habitat/ecosystem protection within park boundaries. Present-tense protection wording avoids unsupported attribution of the present marine scope to its creation in 1980, given expansion in 1984 at L62.

literalGroups.literal: Рантхамбор — индийский парк в Раджастхане, известный наблюдениями за бенгальскими тиграми у старинной крепости.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The literal asserts an Indian park in Rajasthan, Bengal tiger viewing and a historic fort. Search results are promising discovery, but the original page body and one official alternative both timed out; only navigation survived. No full claim-bearing official primary context was read, so these assertions are not qualified in this packet.

literalGroups.literal: Читван — непальский парк в тераях с однорогими носорогами и бенгальскими тиграми.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO describes Chitwan at the foot of the Himalayas in the Terai at L5 and locates it in Nepal at L48-L49; single-horned rhinoceros and Bengal tiger are explicitly named at L5,L48,L58. This is a positive fact about Chitwan, not an explanation copied from the Galápagos key.

absoluteDifficulty.ground: Галапагосы и гигантские черепахи/Дарвин — широкая школьная и культурная ассоциация, не редкая дата. Эквадор даёт дополнительную географическую подсказку; остальные варианты — реальные национальные парки с крупной фауной. Эта оценка уровня не отменяет MAIN-дубль и неполное доказательство варианта2.

defects.ground: islands-013 asks Galápagos from Darwin observations plus giant tortoises. NP17 repeats recognition of the same archipelago through giant tortoises and Darwin-associated finches; Ecuador and the national-park label do not create a new conservation relation. Marine iguana is another clue to the same recognition, not a separate asked fact.
defects.next: A concrete new protected-nature MAIN fact, independently sourced and broad-adult easy, is required; do not apply the minor note repair as a qualified full card.
